items.title: Nurses report an ‘increase in deaths and maggots in wounds’ amid summer heatwave
items.summary: Nurses report an ‘increase in deaths’ during the summer heatwave, finding maggots in wounds and cancer patients ‘dripping with sweat’, a survey has revealed.

items.title: What’s the harm?
items.summary: I am increasingly starting to wonder if we are too busy to ask the really difficult questions that may challenge our accepted norms.

items.title: From critical appraisal to critical thinking
items.summary: In my last editorial, I explored how structured appraisal tools, such as the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP, 2026) and Joanna Briggs Institute checklists (JBI, 2026), can help to provide a structured approach to evaluating evidence in wound care.

items.title: Stakeholder perspectives on the role of economic evidence in decision-making for diabetes-related foot ulcer treatments
items.summary: Dear Editor, Diabetes-related foot ulcers (DFUs) represent a major clinical and economic burden for patients and healthcare systems (Armstrong et al, 2017; Kerr et al, 2019; Edmonds et al, 2021). Economic evaluations are increasingly encouraged to inform adoption and reimbursement decisions for DFU interventions.

items.title: Feeling invisible in a world of seniors and people with limited mobility: The lived experience
items.summary: “Now I sit here on this bench all day and never get a glance,My steps are slow, my hair is grey, near the end of life’s sweet dance…It seems my childhood wish was granted, invisibility” – James T Atkins, from his poem Invisibility.

items.title: Top ten tips: Sharing your work
items.summary: One of the easiest ways to start to share your work is to submit a conference abstract.

items.title: Understanding the factors influencing clinicians’ adoption of Moisture-Associated Skin Damage (MASD) Best Practice Guidance: A qualitative interview study
items.summary: This article presents findings from semi-structured interviews with healthcare professionals and explores the factors that support or hinder clinicians in implementing the 2025 MASD Best Practice Statement within clinical settings.

items.title: Building specialist capability: Developing a proficiency-based induction for tissue viability services
items.summary: There is a truism that a well-planned recruitment and selection process helps organisations avoid the challenges of under- or over-staffing, a pressing issue in today’s climate of reduced nursing staff numbers.

items.title: Targeted postoperative wound care kits delivered as part of digital surgical site infection surveillance after cardiac surgery: Early findings from a quality improvement project
items.summary: After surgery, around 20% of patients develop a wound healing concern, such as dehiscence, seroma, haematoma or infection (Guest et al, 2015). These complications may be expensive to treat and have poor clinical outcomes for patients.

items.title: Understanding arterial duplex scanning in lower-limb ulcer care: A practical guide for community nurses and tissue viability teams
items.summary: Lower limb ulceration is commonly managed within community settings, where nurses and tissue viability teams are often the first clinicians to identify underlying arterial disease (Pagnamenta et al, 2024).

items.title: Multimodal wound care in infection continuum management: Supporting antimicrobial stewardship through early intervention
items.summary: Chronic wounds frequently fail to progress through the normal stages of healing despite appropriate treatment. A principal reason is microbial burden.

items.title: Clinical and health economic benefits of a wound bed-conforming silicone foam dressing with 3DFit Technology – A literature review
items.summary: Wound exudate contains various components, such as nutrients, inflammatory mediators, matrix metalloproteinases and immune cells, which play key roles in wound healing (World Union of Wound Healing Societies [WUWHS], 2019).

items.title: The role of the Care Quality Commission in clinical practice: Delivering safe, person-centred lower-limb care in acute and community settings
items.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC) serves as the independent regulator of health and social care services in England, collaborating with care providers, service users and wider system partners to promote high-quality, safe and effective care (CQC, 2026).

items.title: The impact of toxic leaders
items.summary: In the previous paper, toxic leadership was described as a destructive pattern of behaviour in which leaders act in self-serving ways, undermine others and create environments in which staff feel controlled, blamed and unsafe (Ellis, 2026).

items.title: Authenticity: The hidden quest
items.summary: They always say that you write the book that you are meant to read, and I feel as though I have been humbled in that process as my first book prepares for release next month (Molyneux, 2026).

items.title: Legs Matter Week 2026 showed us that it doesn’t have to be this way
items.summary: From 8-12 June 2026, healthcare professionals, patients, carers, organisations and advocates came together for the seventh annual Legs Matter Week. This year’s theme, It doesn’t have to be this way, shone a spotlight on a simple but powerful message: when guideline-based care is implemented, outcomes improve.

items.title: Supporting Leg Clubs with a benchmark process
items.summary: The non-medical psychosocial Leg Club Model approach to lower limb care has proven to be a very cost-effective way of treating conditions of the lower limb, especially leg ulcers which have often led to social isolation and a lower quality of life for elderly sufferers.

items.title: Made Easy: Zinc oxide and ichthammol, A new approach to managing category 1 and 2 pressure ulcers and moisture-associated skin damage
items.summary: Promoting wound healing with zinc oxide Zinc is a chemical element that is an essential nutrient for the human body and is involved in growth, immune function, tissue maintenance, skin integrity and wound healing (Kogan et al, 2017; Al-Khafaji et al, 2022).
